links.outcome: Readability (Flesch-Kincaid Grade Level, Reading Ease) of LLM answers to patient hip arthroscopy questions
links.effect: FKGL: ChatGPT 11.0 vs Microsoft 8.6 vs Gemini 6.6 (P=.003); Reading Ease: ChatGPT 36.6 vs Microsoft 57.7 vs Gemini 65.0 (P=.001). ChatGPT worst.
links.quote: ChatGPT responses were at a significantly worse reading level compared to Gemini and Microsoft outputs (Flesch-Kincaid Grade Level mean ± SD: ChatGPT: 11.0 ± 2.2 grade reading level vs Microsoft: 8.6 ± 2.3 vs Gemini: 6.6 ± 2.2, P = .003; Flesch Reading Ease mean ± SD: ChatGPT: 36.6 ± 19.0 vs Microsoft: 57.7 ± 13.3 vs Gemini: 65.0 ± 4.7, P = .001).

links.outcome: Reading grade level of LLM patient-facing responses
links.effect: ChatGPT mean grade level 11.0, Microsoft 8.6, Gemini 6.6 (P=.003); only Gemini approached a typical recommended patient reading level.
links.quote: ChatGPT responses were at a significantly worse reading level compared to Gemini and Microsoft outputs (Flesch-Kincaid Grade Level mean ± SD: ChatGPT: 11.0 ± 2.2 grade reading level vs Microsoft: 8.6 ± 2.3 vs Gemini: 6.6 ± 2.2, P = .003; Flesch Reading Ease mean ± SD: ChatGPT: 36.6 ± 19.0 vs Microsoft: 57.7 ± 13.3 vs Gemini: 65.0 ± 4.7, P = .001).

links.outcome: Expert-graded accuracy and incorrect response rate of LLM answers on hip arthroscopy
links.effect: Mean Likert grades 3.0 (ChatGPT), 2.9 (Microsoft), 2.6 (Gemini), P=.481; overall incorrect response rate among LLMs was 20%.
links.quote: The overall incorrect response rate among LLMs was 20%.

screen.reason: The study evaluates the baseline accuracy, adequacy, and readability of three commercial LLMs responding to hip arthroscopy patient questions without testing any deployment practice or safeguard.
